### Observed differences

- In the later window, A21, A22, A23 and A24 each take part in about 77 of 100 traces, up from about 22 of 100 before (A21: 43 of 200 traces before versus 154 of 200 after); mean occurrences per trace match participation and recurrence is near zero, so these activities still occur at most once per case — the change is in how often they run, not in repetition. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]
- Over the same window, A25, A26, A27 and A28 each drop to about 23 of 100 traces from about 79 of 100 (A25: 157 of 200 before versus 46 of 200 after). [OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008]
- The dominant successor of A20 reverses: before, about 78 of 100 of A20's outgoing transitions led to A28 and about 21 to A24; in the later window, about 77 lead to A24 and about 23 to A28. [DIR001]
- A20's context moves with it: before, A20 preceded A25 in about 78 of 100 traces and co-occurred with A25–A28; in the later window it precedes A21, A22, A23 and A24 in about 76 of 100 traces, while its co-occurrence with A25–A28 falls to about 23 of 100. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008]
- Within the now-dominant group, A24 precedes each of A21, A22 and A23 in about 75–76 of 100 traces, and A21–A23 co-occur in about 77 of 100 traces with no fixed order (each direction roughly 35–40 of 100); the former block keeps a similar mixed internal order but now appears in only about 23 of 100 traces. [REL009, REL010, REL011, REL017, REL018, REL024, REL035]
- The two groups have become nearly mutually exclusive — A21–A24 appear without any of A25–A28 in about 77 of 100 traces, mirroring the roughly 78 of 100 before when A25–A28 appeared without A21–A24 — and A32, present in essentially all traces throughout, now co-occurs with A21–A24 (about 77 of 100) instead of A25–A28. [REL012, REL016, REL019, REL030, REL035, REL038]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the path chosen after A20 flipped between two existing branches: in the later window, most cases leave A20 towards A24 and then run A21–A24 (A24 first, with A21–A23 in variable order), whereas before, most cases left A20 towards A28 and ran A25–A28. Both branches already executed in both windows; what changed is which one carries the majority, shifting from roughly 79/21 to roughly 23/77 between the two groups. [OCC001, OCC005, DIR001, REL001, REL005, REL011, REL035]

The support is direct rather than purely frequency-based: the successor shares of A20 reversed, with A28 falling from about 78% to about 23% of A20's outgoing transitions while A24 rose from about 21% to about 77%. [DIR001]

A20's precedence ties switched from A25–A28 to A21–A24, and the participation of all eight activities moved consistently with this rerouting. [REL001, REL005, OCC001, OCC005]

Fifty-three items qualified in total, many times the roughly one (0.8) expected by chance in an unchanged process, and each item's difference exceeds about 995 of 1,000 random re-splits of the pooled data. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, DIR001, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL030, REL031, REL032, REL033, REL034, REL035, REL036, REL037, REL038, REL039, REL040, REL041, REL042, REL043, REL044]

Limitations: the many relational items largely restate one underlying swap and are not independent confirmations; the windows are finite samples, so differing variant frequencies alone could produce some of this, although a coordinated reversal across eight activities plus a reversed successor profile is hard to attribute to sampling. The evidence also cannot distinguish a modified routing rule at A20 from a shift in the share of cases taking each existing branch, and it cannot show whether the order of A21–A23 was fixed before, because these activities rarely co-occurred in the earlier window. [DIR001, REL009, REL035]
